requirements.title: Choose to operate as a sole proprietorship
requirements.evidence: You’re automatically considered to be a sole proprietorship if you do business activities but don’t register as any other kind of business.
requirements.why: You have 1 owner and chose sole proprietorship. This choice sets how you pay tax and that you and the business are the same legal person.
requirements.background: A sole proprietorship needs no formation filing, so there is nothing to file for this choice.
problems: The quote doesn’t show this requirement: The quote does not say anything about how tax is paid or that owner and business are the same legal person.

requirements.title: Operate as a Texas cottage-food bakery
requirements.agency: Texas Department of State Health Services
requirements.evidence: A cottage food production operation is exempt from the requirements of a food service establishment and does not have to comply with the Texas Food Establishment Rules.
requirements.why: You bake at home and sell cookies, breads and cakes that do not need cold holding. Texas lets this kind of home operation sell without a food-establishment license.

requirements.title: Sell only allowed foods and stay under the sales cap
requirements.agency: Texas Department of State Health Services
requirements.evidence: The CFPO definition has been updated to include nonprofit organizations and increases the annual gross income threshold to $150,000.
requirements.why: You expect $5,000 to $25,000 in first-year sales, which is under the $150,000 cottage-food limit. You must avoid banned foods like meat, seafood, ice, low-acid canned goods, CBD/THC foods, and raw milk.
requirements.background: Your plain cookies, breads and cakes are allowed cottage foods and your expected sales sit well below the state yearly cap, while you avoid banned meats and similar items.
problems: The quote doesn’t show this requirement: The quote shows the $150,000 threshold but does not list any banned foods like meat, seafood, or raw milk.

requirements.title: Complete food-handler training
requirements.agency: Texas Department of State Health Services
requirements.evidence: An individual who operates a cottage food production operation must successfully complete a basic food safety education or training program for food handlers accredited under Health and Safety Code, Chapter 438(D) .
requirements.why: Texas requires every cottage-food operator to finish accredited food-handler training before starting.

requirements.title: Package and label cottage foods the Texas way
requirements.agency: Texas Department of State Health Services
requirements.evidence: Foods sold by a cottage food production operation must be packaged and labeled.
requirements.why: You will sell packaged cookies, breads and cakes in person and at markets. Texas requires safe packaging and a label with your operation name, address or ID, product name, allergens, and the home-produced disclosure.
requirements.background: Texas requires cottage foods to be safely packed with a full label showing your business, product, allergens and the home-made disclosure.
problems: The quote doesn’t show this requirement: The quote says foods must be packaged and labeled but does not show the specific required label contents.

requirements.title: Get a Texas sales and use tax permit
requirements.evidence: There is no fee for the permit, but you may be required to post a security bond.
requirements.why: You will sell tangible goods — cookies, breads and cakes — in Texas at markets and from home. Texas requires sellers of tangible goods to hold a sales-tax permit before selling.
requirements.background: Selling cookies, breads and cakes in Texas means selling tangible goods in the state, which calls for a state sales tax permit before you start.
problems: The quote doesn’t show this requirement: The quote shows there is no fee but does not say sellers of tangible goods must hold a permit before selling.

requirements.title: Handle sales tax correctly on bakery sales
requirements.evidence: Bakery items sold by a business that qualifies as a bakery are not taxable.
requirements.why: Most plain bakery goods for eating later are not taxable, but if you heat items or give eating utensils the sale can become taxable. You need to apply the bakery rule to each sale.
requirements.background: Texas taxes bakery goods differently based on whether the seller qualifies as a bakery and whether items are heated or sold with utensils.
problems: The quote doesn’t show this requirement: The quote says bakery items from a qualifying bakery are not taxable but does not mention heating items or utensils making a sale taxable.

requirements.title: Follow federal food safety and labeling rules if you sell across state lines
conditions: Will you ship orders to customers outside Texas?
requirements.evidence: All labeling of FDA-regulated food products must be truthful and not misleading.
requirements.why: You did not say if you will ship orders. Federal food safety and truthful-labeling rules apply when food is sold across state lines, so shipping would turn them on.
problems: The quote doesn’t show this requirement: The quote requires truthful non-misleading labeling but does not say the rules apply when food is sold across state lines.

requirements.title: Consider getting a federal EIN
requirements.evidence: Beware of websites that charge for an EIN. You never have to pay a fee for an EIN.
requirements.why: As a sole proprietor with no employees you can often use your Social Security number, but a free EIN can help open a bank account and keep your personal number private.
problems: Fee not found in the quote

requirements.title: Register for a state ID to hide your home address on labels
requirements.agency: Texas Department of State Health Services
requirements.evidence: Instead of providing a physical home address on the label, operators may register on the DSHS Online Licensing Registry and place their registration number on the label.
requirements.why: You sell from home and customers pick up at home, and you use a business name instead of your legal name. Registration is optional for non-cold foods but lets you put an ID number on the label instead of your home address.
problems: The quote doesn’t show this requirement: The quote allows using a registration number instead of a home address but does not say registration is optional for non-cold foods.

requirements.title: File Texas sales-tax returns on schedule
requirements.evidence: You are required to file a sales and use tax return even if there are no taxable sales or purchases to report during that filing period.
requirements.why: Once you hold a Texas sales-tax permit you must keep filing returns, even if your bakery sales are nontaxable in that period.

requirements.title: Pay federal self-employment tax
requirements.evidence: Your net earnings from self-employment (excluding church employee income) were $400 or more.
requirements.why: As a sole proprietor you are self-employed. With $5,000 to $25,000 in expected sales you will likely have over $400 in net earnings, which triggers this yearly Social Security and Medicare tax.

requirements.title: Pay quarterly estimated taxes if you will owe enough
requirements.evidence: Individuals, including sole proprietors, partners, and S corporation shareholders, generally must make estimated tax payments if they expect to owe tax of $1,000 or more when their return is filed.
requirements.why: Side bakery income usually has no tax withheld. Whether quarterly payments are needed depends on how much total tax you will owe when you file.

requirements.title: Register for Texas employer taxes if you hire
conditions: Will you hire employees in the future?
requirements.why: You plan no hiring now, so this stays on hold. If you later hire help for baking, markets, or deliveries, Texas employer registration and payroll duties would apply.

requirements.title: File your assumed business name in Travis County
requirements.evidence: The following business entity types must file an assumed name certificate with the county clerk in each county in which they have a business office. Filing fee is $23.00 for business name and one owner.
requirements.why: You are a sole proprietor using Rise & Crumb instead of your own legal name, with your business office at home in Travis County.
requirements.background: Texas expects a sole proprietor who works under a shop name different from the owner legal name to file that name with the county clerk.
problems: Quote not found on the cited pages

requirements.title: Follow Austin home business compatibility rules
requirements.evidence: A home-based business is a business that operates from a residential property, by the owner or tenant of the property, and is used for the purpose of manufacturing, providing, or selling a lawful good or providing a lawful service. The City of Austin cannot prohibit or require permits for home-based businesses that do not exceed occupancy limits, generate significant traffic, or create visible or noise disturbances.
requirements.why: You will bake at home inside Austin and have customers pick up at home, so you must meet the City health, safety and neighborhood compatibility rules.
requirements.background: Austin enforces health, safety and neighborhood compatibility for home businesses, which covers a home bakery with customer pickups.
problems: The quote doesn’t show this requirement: The quote defines a home-based business and limits on city action but does not show a health, safety and compatibility requirement for home baking with pickups.

requirements.title: Get an Austin sign permit if you put up an outdoor business sign
conditions: Will you put up an outdoor sign at your home?
requirements.why: You have home pickups, so you might want an outdoor sign, and Austin requires a permit for outdoor business signs.
problems: The quote doesn’t show this requirement: The quote says something is required for outdoor signage but does not show that an Austin sign permit is required.

requirements.title: Report taxable business equipment to Travis County each year
requirements.why: Home bakeries commonly own business tools and equipment at home, and Texas counties tax business personal property each year.
requirements.background: Texas taxes business equipment separately, and Travis County sets a yearly filing for owners to list that property.

openQuestions.question: We couldn’t find an official page about forming an LLC or other business entity in Texas. That doesn’t mean nothing applies, so ask.
openQuestions.answer: You already chose to work as a sole proprietor, so you do not need to create a separate business entity. If you later want liability protection you could form a Texas entity with the state, but that is a choice not a requirement for this bakery.

openQuestions.question: Our search for official pages about business licenses in Travis County didn’t finish. Re-check later, or ask.
openQuestions.answer: Texas cottage food law bars cities and counties from requiring a local license or permit or fee to make cottage food at home and sell it directly to customers. You still must follow labeling and food rules, but you do not need a county business license for these direct sales.

openQuestions.question: Does a home bakery selling only at markets and from home count as a bakery for Texas sales tax?
openQuestions.answer: Texas treats a shop that mostly sells bakery goods for eating off site as a bakery, and plain cookies and breads for eating later are generally not taxable. Your sales stay nontaxable when you do not heat items and do not hand out plates or utensils with them.

openQuestions.question: Does the small-business exemption from federal nutrition labeling apply at your expected sales level?
openQuestions.answer: The pages provided do not explain federal nutrition labeling or any small business exemption, so this cannot be settled from them. A food labeling specialist or the federal food labeling rules would need to confirm whether your bakery qualifies.

openQuestions.question: Do weekly home pickups for cookies and cakes count as significant traffic that would allow the City to restrict the home business?
openQuestions.answer: The city only restricts home businesses that create noticeable neighborhood impacts such as heavy traffic, noise, or visible signs of business. Occasional quiet pickups are usually fine, but regular customer cars coming and going could be seen as significant, so keep visits few and quiet.

openQuestions.question: Do Austin farmers markets or other in-person sites need any separate city approval for a cottage-food seller who already sells direct to customers?
openQuestions.answer: A cottage baker who sells directly to customers does not need extra city food approval to sell at markets or from home under state cottage law. The market itself may have its own vendor rules and stall requirements, so follow those market rules.

openQuestions.question: What is the current Travis County process and total fee to file and renew an assumed name for one owner, online or in person?
openQuestions.answer: You file an assumed name certificate with the county clerk in person with ID for all owners or by mail with a notarized form, and staff can also check name availability for you. The clerk lists a modest base filing charge with a small extra amount for each added owner and for in-office acknowledgment, so check the current clerk schedule before you go.

conflicts.about: Whether a home business can be visible to neighbors and customers
conflicts.explanation: One city page says home occupations strictly prohibit visible storefronts, on-site signage and exterior business operations, while another says the City cannot prohibit or require permits for home businesses that stay within occupancy, traffic and noise limits. It is unclear if pickup sales and a small sign are allowed by-right today or only in a future pilot area.
